snp2.5:7.2: The banyan is “trunk-born” (_khandhaja_) in two ways. As an epiphyte, it is sometimes called the “strangler fig”, since it grows around the trunk of a previous tree, strangling it. Then the banyan sends out aerial roots from the branches; when they reach the ground they establish themselves as supportive trunks known as “prop roots”, so that even if original trunk dies, the tree survives. Thus the tree itself is “trunk-born” and its multiple prop roots are also “trunk-born”. The gramar and commentary indicate the second sense is meant here. The metaphor is even more apt, since the word _nigrodha_ (“banyan”) means “down-grower”, as the tree grows not to the sky but back into the earth.
